text:
Frederick stared at the glowing runes, the weight of eternity pressing against his mortal heart. The draft intensified, carrying the scent of ozone and ancient dust. He looked at the vial of shimmering liquid he had just prepared, then at the crumbling stone altar that had witnessed centuries of forgotten kings. The temptation was a physical ache, a whisper promising an end to fear, to loss, to time itself. But as he traced the final rune, he realized the text was not a gift, but a warning. The "eternal life" described was not one of vitality, but of stagnation—a soul trapped in a single moment, watching the world rot while he remained unchanged.

With a trembling hand, Frederick did not drink. Instead, he picked up the heavy iron candlestick from the altar. He didn't hesitate. He smashed the vial, watching the precious liquid sizzle and evaporate into harmless gray smoke. Then, he took the book itself, the pages fluttering wildly as if in protest, and threw it into the brazier of hot coals. The runes flared bright orange before curling into ash. The draft ceased. The chamber fell silent. Frederick walked out into the sunlight, leaving the secret behind, choosing the fleeting beauty of a mortal life over the hollow promise of forever.

Christopher Columbus
